title: Lessons with Arthur Horn and the first alto
summary: A boarder, Arthur Horn, taught him for 35 cents a lesson paid in laundry; an uncle's C.G. Conn alto was acquired the same way.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Yes, and I'd like to get back to the very beginning of my association with the instrument. There was a saxophone player living at our house, renting a room. You know, in ...(?)... plenty of rooms, and two beds in one room and all that type of thing. And he lived there with us... So my mother approached him about teaching me to play, giving me lessons. And he was very happy to do it. And they came to an agreement where she washed and ironed his clothes to pay for my lesson, 35 cents per lesson, you know. His name was Arthur Horn. And he taught me everything he was able to teach me, and after about six months he told me that I was on my own, because he didn't know anything else to teach me. I was 11 years old at the time.

So I was pretty much on my own, and practicing out of the books; you know, the original saxophone book, the Ben Barekan(?) -- because all the guys were studying out of that. I think a lot of guys nowadays... In fact, I heard John Coltrane play a passage the other day from that book. [LAUGHS] I noticed some little lines in there. You know, a lot of guys lifted those lines out of that book. There are some pretty good lines in the book.

But anyway, I didn't have an instrument. And my uncle, Philip(?) Reed, he bought an alto saxophone with the intention, you know, of doing big things, and he gave it up after a while -- he didn't stay with it. So my mother made a deal with him to wash and iron his clothes to pay for the saxophone. And he agreed to let me have it, you know. So then I had my own instrument.
It was an alto saxophone, C.G. Conn, ha-ha, alto saxophone.
